Case 1: Predinner Snack Attack

| have the worst sweet tooth. | manage to fight sweet

cravings until | get home, and then | inevitably attack the

chocolate chip cookies. | feel as though I’m powerless and

have no control over sweets. | hope you can put me on the

—David, 47-year-old marathon runner, accountant, and
father
Stories like David's are typical among my clients. He came to me feeling
guilty about his lack of control over sweets. He required about 3,000 calo-
ries per day but ate zero calories at breakfast and barely ate lunch, only
a 200-calorie yogurt, because he claimed he had no time. No wonder he
was uncontrollably ravenous by the time he got home; he had accumulated
a 2,800-calorie deficit! Nature took control by encouraging him to eat
more than enough so that he would get adequate energy into his system.
| suggested that David eat his 1,600 cookie calories in the form of whole-

some meals during the day. He started eating 800 calories for breakfast
(cereal, milk, banana, and an english muffin with almond butter) and
1,000 calories of easy-to-eat snack-type foods for lunch and throughout
the afternoon (two yogurts, two large bananas, two protein bars). Within
one day he discovered that he wasn’t a cookie monster after all. He could
